rounds.response: If you are quiet in meetings, simply demonstrate engagement by taking notes, making eye contact, and saying, "I'm just taking it all in right now," if someone asks for your input. When you inevitably forget a name, address it immediately and politely by saying, "I'm so sorry, I've met so many people this week—could you remind me of your name?" If you realize you've asked a basic question, don't apologize profusely; instead, say, "Thanks for clarifying, I just want to ensure I'm aligned with how things are done here." For any other minor, awkward missteps, just smile and say, "Thanks for bearing with me while I learn the ropes." Handling these moments with lighthearted honesty rather than defensiveness shows confidence and makes you highly approachable to your new coworkers.
